_comment: L1 example-selection contract. Python filters the skill's examples per utterance (`select_examples`), keeping one clarify example, one reject example and up to three domain examples ranked by overlap with the retrieved tools; native shipped the whole block unfiltered. For ffmpeg that is 28 examples against the reference's 5. Given (examples, retrieved tool names, query) both runtimes must select the same examples, in the same order, and render the same block. Consumed by python/core/tests/test_example_selection_parity.py and `example_selection_parity_cases` in native/crates/knaif-core/tests/parity.rs.
_stage: The stage is `select_examples -> render_examples_block`, the block that reaches the model — not the selection alone. Python composes it in CommandAgent.build_prompt, native in PlanSession::plan. Comparing the selection without the rendering would violate Rule 2.
_expected_values: Produced by the reference runtime (knaif.prompt.select_examples then render_examples_block). DO NOT regenerate to make a failing test pass. The `shipped` section is a golden over the real skill bundles: if a prompt.yaml changes, regenerating is correct — that is the drift signal working.

cases.name: the_domain_slots_fill_even_with_no_overlap
cases.why: No retrieved tool matches any example, so every domain example scores (0, 0) -- and three are still selected. The cap is a cap, not a relevance threshold; a native port that filtered on overlap > 0 would send the model a clarify/reject pair and nothing else.

cases.name: domain_examples_rank_by_retrieved_tool_overlap
cases.why: The two examples whose plans use a retrieved tool outrank the four that do not.
cases.query: turn the video and mute it

cases.name: the_domain_cap_is_three
cases.why: Five domain examples match; max_tool_examples caps the selection at three.

cases.name: a_two_tool_example_outranks_a_one_tool_example
cases.why: Tool overlap is the primary key: the chain example overlaps two retrieved tools.

cases.name: query_token_overlap_breaks_a_tool_overlap_tie
cases.why: Four examples tie at one retrieved tool; the request sharing query words wins.

cases.name: equal_scores_keep_corpus_order
cases.why: All four score (1, 0). Python's sorted(reverse=True) is stable, so the first three in corpus order survive the cap — a reversed sort would keep the last three.

cases.name: selection_is_re_emitted_in_corpus_order
cases.why: The strip_audio example ranks first but is emitted after the earlier-declared ones.

cases.name: a_done_only_example_is_never_selected
cases.why: `done` is terminal: the example has no domain tool and is neither clarify nor reject.

cases.name: a_clarify_example_that_also_calls_a_tool_is_a_domain_example
cases.why: The fixed clarify slot takes the pure-clarify example; the mixed one competes on rank.

cases.name: a_corpus_with_no_reject_example_fills_only_the_slots_it_has
cases.why: No reject example exists; nothing is invented to fill the slot.

cases.name: an_empty_corpus_selects_nothing
cases.why: Callers fall back to the unfiltered block when the selection is empty.
